brief: Two Goldman desk strategists reach opposite conclusions from the same week: Alphabet's worst-ever one-day drop, Intel's record crash and a weak Amazon print pushed the Nasdaq 100 into correction, yet the S&P 500 ended October down under 1% while the S&P ex-AI index had its best month since 2022. Tony Pasquariello argues S&P earnings growth has peaked and forward-estimate upgrades have slowed, so the bull trend survives but with less upside power and he is making no big bets. Mark Wilson counters that Google Cloud's and AWS's combined $1.1 trillion cloud backlog, plus financing moves from Meta, Oracle and SpaceX, answer the AI ROI question and shrink the funding gap. The piece's own rebuttal: Alphabet's backlog came with negative free cash flow, zero buybacks, new stock and bond sales, and hyperscaler off-balance-sheet obligations up $1 trillion in 90 days to $4.1 trillion, with Blackstone questioning Anthropic's investment-grade prospects. It concludes the week's price action sided with Pasquariello's caution.
